approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a three-bill package that would let the Commonwealth recover costs for indirect biosecurity services under the Biosecurity Bill.
It amends the Quarantine Charges (Imposition-Customs) Act 2014 to allow charges for such services when they are considered customs duties under section 55 of the Constitution.
The bill is enabling and mechanistic, mirroring the General Amendment Bill, and does not set charge amounts or impose financial impacts on businesses.
Enables the imposition of charges for indirect biosecurity services where the charge is a customs duty.
Mirrors the provisions of the Quarantine Charges (Imposition-General) Amendment Bill 2014.
Users of the biosecurity system and businesses that may be subject to charges, though the bill itself imposes no financial impacts.

Introduced the Quarantine Charges (Imposition-Customs) Amendment Bill 2014, the second of three charging bills supporting the Biosecurity Bill package, which will impose charges only when they are considered a duty of customs.

Summed up the Biosecurity Bill debate, noting the Quarantine Act has been amended more than 50 times over 106 years and Australia's agricultural production was worth $53 billion in 2013 to 2014, and assured the House the Inspector-General of Biosecurity position and its funding, currently held by Dr Michael Bond, will continue.
